title: Your profile
text: Everything about you in one place: who you are, what you bring, what you share of it – and the comparison with people you are connected to.

identity.title: Who you are
identity.text: These details apply everywhere in CoFoundery – in your founder profile, in co-founder search and in Connect. You only maintain them here.
identity.name: Name
identity.headline: Headline
identity.headlineHint: One sentence saying what you do.
identity.bioHint: What should people know about your work?
identity.regionHint: Roughly is enough: Berlin, Rhine-Main, North Rhine-Westphalia.
identity.publishedNote: Your Connect profile is published. Changes here are visible there immediately.
identity.rolesHint: This controls which areas are offered to you – not what you have access to. Advisor insight stays tied to the teams that invited you.

roles.founder: Founder – I am founding or looking to

identity.publishNote: You can save at any time – this only applies if you want your profile visible to others in Connect or in co-founder search.

gaps.displayName: A name with at least {min} characters
gaps.headline: A headline with at least {min} characters
gaps.bio: A text about you with at least {min} characters

identity.photoVisibleLabel: Make my photo visible to signed-in members
identity.photoVisibleHint: Your CoFoundery profile photo then appears wherever members see you – in the co-founder search, in connections and in teams. Without this, only you see it. It does not apply to Connect: public pages hang off that, so you decide the photo there separately.

linkedin.title: LinkedIn
linkedin.urlHint: The address of your profile. You can paste it straight from the address bar – we'll add the “https://”. LinkedIn only, no other addresses.
linkedin.urlInvalid: We don't recognise that as a LinkedIn profile. It needs to be an address at linkedin.com, for example linkedin.com/in/your-name.
linkedin.visibilityTitle: Who should see your LinkedIn profile?

private.label: Nobody but you
private.hint: The address is saved but shown nowhere. Useful if you want it on file and decide later.

contacts.label: People you are connected to
contacts.hint: Only those who accepted a contact request with you – people you are already talking to anyway.

members.label: Everyone signed in to CoFoundery
members.hint: Anyone with an account here who is logged in. Not out on the open web, but not just your closest circle either.

public.label: Outside CoFoundery too
public.hint: On your public network page, which anyone can open without an account.

linkedin.publicWarning: Anyone on the internet can open that page, and search engines read it. Your LinkedIn profile would become findable under your name.
linkedin.publicConfirm: Yes, my LinkedIn profile may appear on my public page.
linkedin.openHint: Opens LinkedIn in a new window

cv.title: Read in your CV (optional)
cv.betaNote: Still beta: for now it only works by copy and paste – welcome back to the 2000s 😉 Reading files directly is coming soon.
cv.text: Paste your CV as text. The tool marks which skills and industries it recognises in it – you decide what makes it into your profile.
cv.privacyNote: Your CV stays in your browser. It is not uploaded, not sent to an AI, and not stored anywhere. Once you leave the page it's gone.
cv.placeholder: Paste it here – Ctrl+A, Ctrl+C in your PDF, then Ctrl+V here.
cv.tooShort: That's still too little text to find anything meaningful. Go ahead and paste the whole CV.
cv.nothingFoundHint: That says nothing about your career – the method only knows a fixed list of words. Just enter your skills and industries yourself above.
cv.applied: Applied – check the fields above, then save.
cv.fileUnsupported: We can't read that file. Plain text only (.txt or .md) – for a PDF or Word document, copy the contents straight into the field.

evidence.title: What was the last piece of work you owned and saw through?
evidence.text: A concrete example says more about your experience than a list of keywords. It does not have to come from a job – your own project, volunteering or freelance work counts just as much.
evidence.narrativeLabel: What was it, and what was yours to carry?
evidence.narrativePlaceholder: For example: I took our first enterprise customer from the first approach to a signed contract – the proposal, the follow-up questions and the negotiation were mine.
evidence.narrativeHint: Two or three sentences are enough. At least {min} characters.
evidence.levelLabel: And how much experience do you have in that area overall?
evidence.assignmentNote: I will suggest which area that is in the next step – confirming it is up to you.

confirm.title: Here is what I read into it
confirm.text: I only go by terms in your text – that can fit well and it can be off. So I would rather ask: which of these was genuinely your strength?
confirm.noneIsFine: If none of these fit, simply pick nothing. You can set the area yourself in the next step.
confirm.emptyTitle: This is where I get stuck
confirm.emptyText: I could not derive an area from your text. That says nothing about your description – my list of terms is limited and does not catch paraphrases. You will pick the area yourself in the next step.

engine.rules: Assigned from a fixed list of terms inside your browser, without an AI model. Your text is not transmitted for this.
engine.model: Assigned by an AI model. The result can be wrong – your selection is what counts.

areas.title: Which other areas have you worked in?
areas.text: Start with the fields you have actually worked in. The specific areas appear afterwards. Focus on what matters rather than everything you have touched once.

ownership.title: Which of these do you not want to own long term?
ownership.text: Being able to do something does not mean wanting to be responsible for it. Settling that distinction early saves a lot of misunderstanding later.
ownership.noEntries: You have not selected any areas yet.

levels.label: Experience
levels.5: Applied in demanding situations too, can support others

ownershipWishes.label: Ownership
ownershipWishes.grow_into: I want to grow into it
ownershipWishes.prefer_external: I would rather cover it externally

summary.title: What you bring
summary.empty: Your picture appears here once you have filled in the snapshot.
summary.incompleteNote: Anything not listed here only means you have not entered it yet.
summary.removeEvidenceQuestion: Really remove this evidence? The text will be gone.

readout.title: What can be read from this
readout.coverage: {areas} areas recorded, {levelled} of them with an experience level and {wished} with an ownership preference.
readout.basis: This readout only places your own entries side by side – experience level and ownership preference. It reads nothing into them, and an empty field only means nothing is written there.

anchor.title: This is where you want to carry the responsibility
anchor.text: These are the areas you want to be permanently in charge of. In a founding conversation, this is your claim.

canButHandsOver.title: You can do this – you just do not want to keep it
canButHandsOver.text: You stated depth here and still said someone else should own it permanently. That is not a contradiction but the most important input for dividing roles: you can be counted on when it matters, yet this is not your seat.

growingInto.title: This is where you want to grow into it
growingInto.text: Responsibility yes, depth of experience not yet. That can be planned for – once it is said out loud.

contributes.title: Here you contribute without leading it
contributes.text: You get involved but do not want to be in charge. That tends to ease a division of roles rather than restrict it.

undecided.title: Here it is still open what you want
undecided.text: No ownership preference given, or explicitly still unclear. That is a good place for a conversation to start.

comparison.title: If the two of you were to found together
comparison.intro: This is not an assessment and not a compatibility score. It places your entries side by side and sorts them by what should be settled before founding.
comparison.basis: The basis is two self-reports – experience level and ownership preference. This is a conversation starter, not a test instrument, and it does not predict success.
comparison.coverage: {together} areas in total, {shared} of them entered by both of you, {onlyA} only by you, {onlyB} only by {name}.
comparison.gapNote: Where entries are missing, nothing is shown. That can mean: not entered – or not shared. We deliberately do not tell those apart, because otherwise holding back would itself be a statement.

overlap.high: You have both entered something almost everywhere. That means plenty of shared language about the work – and probably shared blind spots too.
overlap.balanced: Your entries overlap in part and complement each other in part.
overlap.low: You have barely entered the same areas. That means a lot of complementarity – and little shared language about what the other one's work looks like.

contested.title: Both of you want to own it
contested.text: You are claiming the same responsibility here. This is the question founding teams usually ask too late – and unsettled responsibility has a measurably poor effect. Settle it before it shows up as conflict.

openPosition.title: Nobody wants to own it
openPosition.text: Neither of you wants to be permanently in charge here. Whether that is a problem depends on what your venture needs – which we do not know. All we say is: it is not filled.

bothShallow.title: Wanted, but without depth yet
bothShallow.text: At least one of you wants to take this on, and neither has stated deep experience here. As a team you are thin at this point.

handoverPath.title: A path that can be planned
handoverPath.text: One of you has depth here and does not want to keep it; the other wants to take it on but is not there yet. That can be planned for – once it is said out loud.

settled.title: This one already sits
settled.text: One of you wants the responsibility and has the experience for it, the other does not want it. Nothing to negotiate here, only to name.

noBasis.title: Not enough to go on
noBasis.text: For these areas there is not enough information to say anything. That is a finding about the data, not about you.

comparison.empty: There is not enough information yet for a comparison with {name}. That may be down to either of your snapshots, or to how far they are shared.
comparison.sectionText: With people you are connected to, you can place your snapshots side by side – ordered by what should be settled before founding.
comparison.noneYet: As soon as a contact request is accepted, that person appears here.

errors.narrative: Please write at least two short sentences.
errors.save: That could not be saved just now. Please try again.
errors.published_incomplete: Your published Connect profile needs a name, a headline and a slightly longer text about you. Please complete the field or set the Connect profile back to draft first.
errors.roles: At least one role has to stay set. Without one, the platform would have no area to take you to.
errors.linkedin: We can't read that as a LinkedIn profile. It has to point to linkedin.com – so we haven't saved it.

contexts.title: Where you decide what is shown
contexts.text: Your details live here. Whether and how they appear in an area is decided there.

disclosure.title: Who gets to see what you can do?
disclosure.text: Above you noted what you have experience in. Here you decide who sees any of it. Until you change something: nobody.
disclosure.privateHint: Your entries stay with you. Others can't even tell that you've filled anything in.
disclosure.areasHint: Your profiles will then show what you have experience in – in your case {examples}, for instance. Nothing more: how much experience you have, and what you'd like to take on, stays with you.
disclosure.areas_depth_on_contact: People you're connected with see more
disclosure.areas_depth_on_contactHint: For everyone else it stays at the topics. Anyone whose connection you've accepted also sees how much experience you have – and what you'd like to take on, and what you'd rather not.
disclosure.note: Two things always hold: nobody ever gets to see your evidence. And on public pages – the ones anyone on the web can open – none of this ever appears.

notices.recognised: We filed your description under one or more areas – already ticked below. Check whether that fits and add what is missing.
notices.unmatched: We could not derive an area from your description yet. It is stored under “Other focus” – pick the area below that actually fits.
notices.confirmed: Your selection is saved. Here you can add whatever is still missing.
